title: Singleton masses of a finite probability space sum to one
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, so that $\Omega$ is finite and discrete and its canonical volume measure $\mathbb{P}$ is a probability measure, and let $\alpha$ be a finite type equipped with a bijection $e : \Omega \xrightarrow{\sim} \alpha$. Then the family of singleton masses $\bigl(\mathbb{P}(\{e^{-1}(a)\})\bigr)_{a \in \alpha}$ is summable with sum $1$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space (finite, discrete, and carrying a probability measure)
e is a bijection Ω ≃ α
replaced:
For any bijection $e : \Omega \xrightarrow{\sim} \alpha$ with $\alpha$ finite, the
family $a \mapsto \mathrm{volume}(\{e^{-1}(a)\})$ has sum $1$ as an $\mathtt{HasSum}$
statement.
